title: Web Proxy Auto Discovery
author: NTT Security - Axel Olsson, Patrik Olson
description: The Web Proxy Auto Discovery (WPAD) protocol attempts to auto-discover proxy settings and is used by e.g. web browsers to make it easier to get a working Internet connection. WPAD uses either the computer's domain name or DNS suffix (configured in Windows) or the domain name found in the DHCP lease (configured in the router/DHCP server) to look for a proxy configuration file 'wpad.dat' which is the same as a PAC file. If the host or router is configured with a domain that is not owned by the user/customer, then the owner of that domain can serve a malicious PAC file and intercept all HTTP traffic from the host (including HTTPS traffic if an HTTP downgrade attack is possible). Try to verify that the domain is registered and not parked, and examine the contents of the file if it exists.
